s: Who among the following was the sole revolutionary of the “Kakori Conspiracy Case” who escaped from arrest by the police?

The treasury of Government was looted by this organization at Kakori, a place in Lucknow-Saharanpur section on 9 August, 1925 A.D. This incident is known as Kakori Conspiracy (Kakori Train Action). 43 revolutionaries were arrested in which Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged while Azad and others escaped. Azad was the key member of HRA who was never arrested by the British Government.

s: Under whose chairmanship a committee was formed to defend the accused in Kakori Case?
x: Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee was one of the founder members of Hindustan Republican Association. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in Kakori Case (Kakori train action). He wrote in his book ‘In search of Freedom’ that Pandit Motilal Nehru under Leadership of Govind Ballabh Pant formed the Kakori Case (Kakori train action day) Defense Committee. In an article by Shankar Narayan Rao at PIB website, it is mentioned that in this case President of the defence committee was Pandit Motilal Nehru. We at this moment considering Shri Chatterjee's book as a primary source consider option (b) as the correct answer. Initially, UPPSC has considered option (d) as the correct option, but later on in its revised answer sheet it supports option (b) as the correct answer.

Who among the following organised the famous Chittagong armoury raid?
x: Surya Sen, popularly known as Masterda, organised the famous Chittagong Armoury Raid on 18 April 1930 in Bengal (now in Bangladesh). The objective of the raid was to seize British arms, disrupt communication networks, and challenge British authority through armed revolution.

s: Who among the following female revolutionary fired at the English Governor (Chancellor) while receiving her degree at the convocation?
x: Two Bengali school girls Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Chaudhary murdered a district magistrate by firing in December, 1931. Bina Das fired at the English Governor while receiving her degree at the convocation in February, 1932 A.D.

s: Who is related to 'Chittagong Armoury Raid'?
x: Chittagong armoury raid was an attempt to raid the armoury of the police and auxiliary forces at Chittagong in Bengal. It was organised by Surya Sen who was also famous by the name of ‘’Master Da’’ The Indian Republican Army (IRA) was established by Surya Sen in Bengal and on 18th April, 1930 A.D., the plan was put into implementation by the members of IRA namely Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath, Nirmal Sen, Ambika Chakrobarty, Naresh Roy, Kalpana Dutt, Anand Gupta, Tegrabal etc. including Surya Sen. Struggle took place on 22nd April, 1930 A.D. between members of Government forces and members of IRA in which 80 soldiers and 12 revolutionaries were killed. On 16 February, 1933 A.D., Surya Sen was arrested and put through legal proceedings and ultimately hanged on 12th January, 1934 A.D.
